name: Mathematics
description: Example graph validated against the custom-schema bundle (Mathematics ontology): a number-theory slice with a theorem, its proof, a refuted conjecture, a problem with solution steps, and the formal/benchmark layer.

elements.name: Euclid
elements.description: The researcher/prover (actor) who studies number theory and solved the infinitude problem.

elements.name: Number Theory
elements.description: The branch of mathematics studying the integers and primes.

elements.name: Integer
elements.description: The set Z of whole numbers.

elements.name: Prime Number
elements.description: An integer greater than 1 with no positive divisors other than 1 and itself.

elements.name: Definition of a Prime Number
elements.description: n > 1 is prime iff its only positive divisors are 1 and n.

elements.name: Well-Ordering Principle
elements.description: Every non-empty set of positive integers has a least element.

elements.name: Euler's Polynomial is Always Prime
elements.description: Conjecture: n^2 + n + 41 is prime for every non-negative integer n.

elements.name: Infinitude of the Primes
elements.description: There are infinitely many prime numbers.

elements.name: Proof by Contradiction
elements.description: Assume the negation and derive a contradiction.

elements.name: Euclid's Proof of the Infinitude of the Primes
elements.description: Assume finitely many primes p1..pn; then N = p1*...*pn + 1 is divisible by none of them, contradiction.

elements.name: n = 40 refutes Euler's Polynomial
elements.description: At n = 40, n^2 + n + 41 = 1681 = 41^2 is composite.

elements.name: Prove There Are Infinitely Many Primes
elements.description: A number-theory problem to be solved.

elements.name: Assume Finitely Many Primes
elements.description: Suppose the primes are exactly p1, ..., pn.

elements.name: Construct N = p1*...*pn + 1
elements.description: Build a number coprime to every assumed prime to reach a contradiction.

elements.name: Constructive Contradiction
elements.description: The competency to build a witness that contradicts a finiteness assumption.

elements.name: Mathlib (Lean 4)
elements.description: The Lean 4 mathematical library holding the formalized statement and proof.

elements.name: miniF2F
elements.description: A formal theorem-proving benchmark spanning olympiad and high-school mathematics.
